title: Explainable Machine Learning for Broadband Adoption Disparities: Tract-Level Prediction and SHAP-Based Factor Profiling
abstract: arXiv:2608.29110v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The United States has allocated approximately $65 billion through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act for broadband expansion, yet evidence-based methods for targeting these investments remain underdeveloped. This paper presents an explainable machine learning framework for profiling broadband adoption disparities at census-tract granularity across 83,359 tracts nationwide. Using 65 socioeconomic, demographic, and infrastructure features derived from the American Community Survey 2022, we train a LightGBM model under spatial five-fold cross-validation, achieving R^2 = 0.533 and Spearman rho = 0.763; state-held-out cross-validation (51 folds) confirms generalization (R^2 = 0.525). TreeSHAP analysis identifies income and education as the dominant factor group (with the engineered interaction term absorbing attribution from its constituent features), and SHAP-based clustering reveals three exploratory factor profiles: Well-Connected

translated_title: 面向宽带普及差异的可解释机器学习：人口普查区级预测与基于SHAP的因素画像
translated_abstract: 美国通过《基础设施投资和就业法案》拨款约650亿美元用于宽带扩展，然而针对这些投资的循证决策方法仍不完善。本文提出了一个可解释的机器学习框架，在全国83,359个人口普查区的粒度上刻画宽带普及差异。基于美国社区调查（ACS）2022年数据提取的65个社会经济、人口统计和基础设施特征，我们在空间五折交叉验证下训练了LightGBM模型，取得了R² = 0.533和Spearman ρ = 0.763的性能；留州交叉验证（51折）证实了模型的泛化能力（R² = 0.525）。TreeSHAP分析识别出收入和教育为主导因素组（其中工程化构建的交互项吸收了其组成特征的归因），基于SHAP的聚类揭示了三种探索性因素画像：良好连接型（Well-Connected）……
tldr: 本文提出一个基于LightGBM与SHAP的可解释机器学习框架，在美国83,359个人口普查区层面预测宽带普及差异，识别出收入和教育为主导因素，为650亿美元宽带投资的精准靶向提供决策依据。
en_tdlr: This paper presents an explainable machine learning framework using LightGBM and SHAP to predict broadband adoption disparities across 83,359 U.S. census tracts, identifying income and education as the dominant factors to guide targeted allocation of the $65 billion broadband expansion investment.
